title: Darwin's theory of evolution
subject: sciences
description: In 1859, Darwin published The Origin of Species. The central idea: living things change over time by natural selection.

hero.hook: Species are not fixed. They change. Slowly. But surely.

blocks.text: In **1859**, **Charles Darwin** published *On the Origin of Species*. The book shocks, fascinates, divides. Its central idea is, however, simple to formulate.
Living things vary. Some variations help survive and reproduce. These variations are transmitted. Over generations, populations change.

As a young boy, Darwin leaves on the ship **Beagle**. For years, he observed plants, fossils, birds. In the Galapagos Islands, he noticed that nearby birds had different beaks depending on their food.

blocks.caption: Nozzles adapted to different diets: a strong indicator.

blocks.text: Imagine a population of animals. Some run a little faster, digest a little better, resist the cold a little more. If it helps them survive and have young, these traits become more common.
It’s not that individuals “want” to evolve. It's a filter: the environment keeps what works. Darwin calls this **natural selection**.
Darwin waited a long time before publishing. He feared scandal. Another naturalist, **Alfred Russell Wallace**, came to similar ideas: this pushed Darwin to release his book.
In the 19th century, many believed that species were created as they were. To say that they change, and that humans share a history with other animals, shakes up religion and society.
Science is progressing: fossils, the geography of species, then later genetics, confirm the general idea.
We now know that DNA carries variations. We observe evolution in the lab (bacteria, viruses) and in nature. We also fight bacteria resistant to antibiotics: this is live evolution.
Darwin showed that living things evolve by natural selection: traits useful for survival and reproduction spread. Modern genetics has confirmed and clarified this framework.
